rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: A Red X means the motorway lane is closed and drivers must not use it.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Red X closures protect people in difficulty and provide access for emergency and recovery services.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Drivers should move into an open lane when directed by lane-change arrows.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Drivers should leave gaps so other vehicles can move safely into open lanes.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: A lane remains closed until signs show that restrictions have ended.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Driving in a Red X lane is illegal and dangerous.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: A hard shoulder must not be used when overhead signals are blank unless it is opened as a running lane.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Police may issue fines and penalty points for Red X or hard-shoulder misuse.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Red-X risk depends on incident location, traffic flow, visibility, compliance, emergency access and road-operating conditions.

rows.source: National Highways Red X and hard-shoulder safety
rows.verified: Red-X evidence is motorway-, lane-, incident-, driver- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Registered medical practitioners must report suspected notifiable diseases to UKHSA.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Urgent suspected cases must be reported by telephone to the local health protection team within 24 hours.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: All suspected cases should be submitted through the online service within 3 days.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Reporting must not wait for laboratory confirmation.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Laboratories with a primary diagnostic role must report confirmed notifiable organisms.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Reports support contact tracing, outbreak management, diagnostic support and trend detection.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Other significant infections or public-health hazards can also be reported for assessment.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: UKHSA publishes current notifications and causative-agent surveillance reports.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: Notification value depends on clinical suspicion, reporting timeliness, diagnostic completeness, case definition and follow-up.

rows.source: UKHSA notifiable disease and organism reporting
rows.verified: NOIDs evidence is report-, disease-, laboratory-, jurisdiction- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
